speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I am Dr. Agent; I need to carefully evaluate your skin condition to rule out any serious underlying issues. Can you tell me exactly what you notice about the lesion, such as its size, color, and if it is changing?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that history, Mr. 62; your history of heavy smoking and the specific location of these non-healing, crusty lesions are concerning. Given the similarity between the penile and digital lesions, have you noticed any bleeding, itching, or pain, and has the size or shape of these spots changed recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (penile and cutaneous).

The patient's history of heavy smoking, African origin, and non-healing, painless, crusty lesions on the penile shaft and finger are highly suggestive of Squamous Cell Carcinoma.

REQUEST TEST: Penile_biopsy and Finger_biopsy.
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermoscopy of penile and digital lesions.
